answer: An agent economy can make voting power grow with the square root of locked stake, not with identity count: one honest agent staking a hundred coins wields ten votes on its long voyage of honest trades, while a sybil farmer splitting the same hundred coins across a thousand puppets gets only a relic of a vote per fake. Each fake’s pulse of influence stays tiny because the square root punishes splitting, and buying real stake for every fake costs a thousand times more than the fraud earns.
